section_summary: Pages 1-68 cover postwar US State Department handling of Japanese narcotics control, 1944-1948. They include a 1948 Moorhead letter and notes urging narcotics provisions in the Japanese peace treaty, and a 1944 League of Nations note on Japan's drug system. They also hold SCAP occupation directives of 1945, and War Crimes Office requests via the Geneva consulate for League evidence on Japanese treaty violations and penalties. The section ends with League circulars, Permanent Central Opium Board correspondence and a blank statistical form.

subfiles.about: Cover letter sending notes on narcotics control in Japan after an unofficial discussion.
subfiles.from: Mrs. Howell Moorhead, Foreign Policy Association
subfiles.summary: Moorhead encloses her notes on Japanese narcotics control following their informal talk two months earlier.
subfiles.title: Moorhead letter to Hamilton

subfiles.about: Proposes that the peace treaty reaffirm drug conventions and keep occupation controls.
subfiles.summary: Citing UN Narcotics Commission recommendations, she urges reaffirming drug conventions, continuing occupation legislation, and prohibiting drug manufacture and export. A control body would include a drugs section and imports would need Permanent Central Opium Board clearance.
subfiles.title: Notes on narcotics control in Japan peace treaty

subfiles.about: Narcotics Commission proposals on controlling narcotics in Japan after the peace treaty.
subfiles.summary: The Commission agreed Japan should have no drug exports or manufacture, imports limited to medical needs with Permanent Central Board endorsement, and domestic control as good as the military system. China asked that recommendations reach treaty-making powers quickly.
subfiles.title: UN ECOSOC Annex: Control of Narcotics in Japan

subfiles.about: Refers to a War Department letter attaching a report by T/Sgt. Johnstone.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to file 711.94114a/1-545, a War Department letter on Johnstone's report.
subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet: Johnstone report

subfiles.about: Sends thirty copies of the note on drug control in Japan for distribution.
subfiles.summary: Steinig transmits 30 copies of O.C. Special 22 and lists how Morlock should distribute them to agencies and military schools.
subfiles.title: Steinig letter to Morlock

subfiles.about: Survey of Japan's drug conventions, laws, controls, production, trade, addiction, penalties and illicit traffic.
subfiles.from: Drug Control Service, League of Nations Secretariat
subfiles.summary: Describes Japan's ratifications, Opium Law and ordinances, Welfare Ministry control, opium and coca production, licensed manufacturers, and statistics for 1935-1939. It also covers addiction, penalties, and evidence of large illicit traffic originating in Japan and Japanese activity in China.
subfiles.title: League note: Drug situation and control in Japan (O.C. Special 22)

subfiles.about: Division of International Labor receipt stamp for Commissioner Anslinger.
subfiles.summary: Routing stamp for narcotics papers.
subfiles.title: Division routing stamp, Anslinger

subfiles.about: Orders prohibiting narcotic cultivation, import, export and manufacture and freezing stocks.
subfiles.summary: Prohibits narcotic plant growth, imports without authorization, exports and manufacture; destroys existing crops; freezes stocks; keeps records; defines terms.
subfiles.title: SCAP memorandum: Control of narcotics

subfiles.about: States narcotics policy for Korea and Japan and requests information on stocks and production.
subfiles.from: GHQ SCAP Public Health and Welfare Section
subfiles.summary: Prohibits growth, export and manufacture, allowing imports only for medical needs; requests statements of stocks, plants and annual narcotics figures 1930-1945.
subfiles.title: SCAP PH&W memorandum on narcotics policy

subfiles.about: Requests League copies of unpublished documents on Japanese narcotics traffic for the War Crimes Office.
subfiles.summary: Asks the League Drug Service for all unpublished documents on Japanese licit and illicit narcotics traffic.
subfiles.title: Telegram to Geneva requesting League documents

subfiles.about: Requests a table comparing Japanese narcotic penalties with about ten other countries.
subfiles.summary: Asks the League Drug Service for a comparison of average penalties for the War Crimes Office.
subfiles.title: Telegram to Geneva requesting penalty table

subfiles.about: Encloses a conversation memorandum and asks State to give Lt. Col. McAnally the information he needs.
subfiles.summary: Treasury requests that State furnish pertinent information to the War Crimes Office.
subfiles.title: Treasury letter to Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Anslinger recommends ten steps to gather evidence for indicting Japan for narcotics treaty violations.
subfiles.summary: Recommends obtaining opium export records from Bushire, Japanese production and import data, Tientsin heroin licenses, a Chinese film, League reports, and Consulate reports. Concludes the evidence would prove Japan violated the conventions.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of conversation: War Crimes Office and Bureau of Narcotics

subfiles.about: Transmits a monograph on pre-war narcotics production and distribution.
subfiles.from: Howard Elting, Jr., American Consul, Geneva
subfiles.summary: Responds to telegram 310; the Board says Japan stopped reporting at the outbreak of hostilities, so the monograph is only of indirect use.
subfiles.title: Geneva despatch transmitting pre-war monograph

subfiles.about: Division receipt stamp for Anslinger.
subfiles.summary: Routing stamp.
subfiles.title: Division routing stamp, Anslinger

subfiles.about: Records Dr. Yosumi's account of weaknesses in Japanese narcotics regulations.
subfiles.from: GHQ SCAP Public Health and Welfare Section
subfiles.summary: Manufacturers report quarterly without licenses, wholesalers and retailers are unlicensed and unreported, and doctors register once and never report.
subfiles.title: SCAP memorandum for record: Dr. Yosumi interview

subfiles.about: Requests an official League statement that Japan stopped submitting required reports after 1939.
subfiles.summary: Asks League authorities for a statement that Japan submitted no illicit traffic reports, annual reports, or estimates after 1939.
subfiles.title: Telegram to Geneva on League statements

subfiles.about: Asks for clarification of the penalties inquiry and country selection.
subfiles.summary: Elting seeks clarification of what penalties means and the purpose of the comparison.
subfiles.title: Incoming telegram from Geneva on penalty table

subfiles.about: Requests statements that Japan never sought revision or denounced the conventions, and clarifies the penalties table.
subfiles.summary: Asks for a League statement on Japan not requesting revision or reporting illicit cases in China, and explains the nine-power penalty table.
subfiles.title: Telegram to Geneva on penalties and Japanese non-action

subfiles.about: Asks whether League drug communications can reach Japanese authorities through the State Department.
subfiles.from: Bertil A. Renborg, League of Nations
subfiles.summary: The Secretariat cannot send official drug communications to Japan and asks State's help.
subfiles.title: Renborg letter to Morlock

subfiles.about: Says there is no objection to forwarding League drug communications to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Consul is to tell Renborg that communications may go to Japan through the Geneva consulate and State Department.
subfiles.title: Instruction to Geneva on League communications

subfiles.about: Transmits Opium Board note and report and despatch 108 for the War Crimes Office.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the Board's December 1945 note, its July 1945 report, and despatch 108.
subfiles.title: State letter to War Department transmitting Geneva material

subfiles.about: Sends the Board's note on Japanese non-fulfilment of obligations.
subfiles.summary: Partly answers telegram 328 with the Board's note. Drug Control Service statement is delayed pending League approval.
subfiles.title: Geneva despatch 106: Permanent Central Opium Board statement

subfiles.about: Details Japan's lapse in reporting under the 1925 and 1931 conventions.
subfiles.from: E. Felkin, Permanent Central Opium Board
subfiles.summary: Japan ceased collaboration after war began; last quarterly returns were 1940, annual returns 1939, estimates 1940, with later dates for territories.
subfiles.title: Permanent Central Opium Board note on Japan

subfiles.about: Reports that the League has no unpublished Japanese traffic documents except Chinese reports.
subfiles.summary: Quotes the Drug Control Service reply, which found only Chinese reports on Japanese-occupied areas, with a list enclosed.
subfiles.title: Geneva despatch 105: Drug Control Service information

subfiles.about: Enclosure listing Chinese reports from 1942-1945.
subfiles.from: Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs / Chinese Legation, Bern
subfiles.summary: Lists items 14-21 on drug conditions in occupied Henan, Hubei, Hunan and other areas.
subfiles.title: List of reports on drug situation in Japanese-occupied China

subfiles.about: Quotes League statement that Japan did not seek revision or denounce the conventions.
subfiles.summary: Renborg confirms the records show no Japanese request for revision of the 1931 Convention or denunciation of the League conventions.
subfiles.title: Geneva despatch 108: League reply on revision or denunciation

subfiles.about: Asks for a report on action on earlier telegrams and speedy statements.
subfiles.summary: Tells Geneva to consult the Drug Service and expedite statements requested in four telegrams.
subfiles.title: Telegram to Geneva urging action

subfiles.about: Reports progress on the Department's requests.
subfiles.summary: Lists answering despatches. Penalty statistics for six countries are prepared and the work should finish by the end of February.
subfiles.title: Incoming telegram from Geneva on status of requests

subfiles.about: Transmits Renborg's reply on Japanese reports.
subfiles.summary: With League approval, encloses Renborg's reply, which with the Board's material fully answers telegram 328.
subfiles.title: Geneva despatch 119: Drug Control Service reply

subfiles.about: States which Japanese reports were not received after 1938-1939.
subfiles.summary: No annual reports after 1938, no illicit traffic reports after 1939, and last estimates were for 1940 or 1941.
subfiles.title: Renborg letter to Elting

subfiles.about: Sends despatches 119 and 122 with a comparative penalties table.
subfiles.summary: Transmits League reply on reports and a table of narcotic penalties in nine countries including Japan.
subfiles.title: State letter to War Department transmitting despatches 119 and 122

subfiles.about: Encloses League circular letters for transmission to the Japanese Government.
subfiles.summary: Lists circulars on dolantin, 1946 estimated requirements, and annual reports.
subfiles.title: Geneva despatch 123: League circulars for Japan

subfiles.about: Transmits a table comparing narcotic penalties in nine countries.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the League table for the War Crimes Office; US legislation is omitted.
subfiles.title: Geneva despatch 122: Comparative penalties table

subfiles.about: Forwards League circular letters for delivery to the Japanese Foreign Office.
subfiles.summary: Encloses circulars on dolantin, estimated requirements and annual reports.
subfiles.title: Instruction to Tokyo forwarding League circulars
subfiles.to: Acting US Political Adviser to SCAP, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Reports that Japan did not report illicit traffic cases in occupied China after 1931.
subfiles.summary: Quotes the Drug Control Service letter, completing the data requested for the War Crimes Office.
subfiles.title: Geneva despatch 131: final League statement

subfiles.about: Sends despatch 131 on Japan's duty to report illicit traffic in China.
subfiles.summary: Says the statement completes the data requested from the Drug Control Service.
subfiles.title: State letter to War Department transmitting despatch 131

subfiles.about: Transmits corrections to the comparative penalties tables.
subfiles.summary: The hastily prepared tables were revised; corrections to Part I, Japan proper, are enclosed.
subfiles.title: Geneva despatch 134: corrections to penalty tables

subfiles.about: Encloses three circular letters for the Japanese Government.
subfiles.from: J. Brock Havron, American Vice Consul
subfiles.summary: Circulars cover import certificates, an Argentine manufacturing authorization, and Demerol.
subfiles.title: Geneva despatch 161: League circulars for Japan

subfiles.about: Asks State to forward the Opium Board letter to the Japanese Foreign Minister.
subfiles.from: Ralph F. Curtiss, War Department Military Intelligence
subfiles.summary: The Commissioner of Narcotics sent the letter to War, which requests State forward it.
subfiles.title: War Department memorandum forwarding Opium Board letter

subfiles.about: Announces closure of the Washington branch office and gives the Geneva address for estimates.
subfiles.summary: Governments should send drug requirement estimates to the Board's President in Geneva.
subfiles.title: Permanent Central Opium Board letter on closing Washington office

subfiles.about: Encloses the Board's letter L.8.L.80-W for appropriate action.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the June 5, 1946 Board letter.
subfiles.title: Instruction to Tokyo forwarding Board letter
subfiles.to: US Political Adviser to SCAP, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Transmits Japan's second-quarter 1946 import and export statistics.
subfiles.summary: Sends Statistical Form A(GL) prepared for the Japanese Government.
subfiles.title: State transmittal of Statistical Form A(GL)
subfiles.to: President, Permanent Central Opium Board, Bern

subfiles.about: Sends Japan's quarterly statistical form for transmission to the Board.
subfiles.summary: Forwards Form A(GL) showing second-quarter 1946 imports and exports.
subfiles.title: Treasury letter forwarding Statistical Form A(GL)
subfiles.to: Division of International Labor, Social and Health Affairs

subfiles.about: Blank form for quarterly narcotics import and export statistics.
subfiles.summary: Form with instructions, notes and tables for drugs by import and export. Entries are largely blank or illegible.
subfiles.title: Statistical Form A(GL) quarterly statistics
